neighbours.label: statements about how well-remembered an artist or work is over time (famous once 'but largely forgotten', 'recently enjoyed a revival'), at the word just before the reputation predicate
fire: Admired by critics throughout the 1920s but largely forgotten since, the sculptor left behind hundreds of bronzes.
The singer was a household name in Brazil but largely unknown to audiences in Europe.
After decades of neglect, her short stories have recently enjoyed a revival among university readers.
A bestseller in its own century but largely unread today, the novel runs to nine hundred pages.
The silent-film director has lately enjoyed a renaissance thanks to restored prints of his comedies.
Praised by his fellow poets in his lifetime but largely ignored afterwards, he died in a rented room.
Her paintings, dismissed for a generation, have recently enjoyed a surge of interest from collectors.
The composer was a celebrity in Vienna but largely overlooked by later historians of music.
quiet: Damaged by fire in the 1920s but largely repaired since, the chapel still holds hundreds of visitors.
The road was finished in Brazil but largely unpaved on the other side of the border.
After decades of drought, the valley farmers have recently enjoyed a wet spring and a good harvest.
A swamp in the last century but largely drained today, the plain runs for nine hundred miles.
The film director has lately enjoyed a long holiday with his family in the mountains.
Planned by the council last year but largely unfunded afterwards, the bridge was never started.
Her paintings, stored for a generation, were recently moved to a dry room by collectors.
The composer was born in Vienna but largely educated at a boarding school in Prague.

notes: Card: 'recognized during his time but⟦⟧ largely forgotten', 'a legend … but largely unknown', 'recently enjoyed a career renaissance', 'is often forgotten'; output promotes ' gaining', ' gained', ' cult', ' niche', ' lesser'. Probes: 'but largely forgotten now' 0.86, 'have recently enjoyed a revival' 0.67; the same words outside reputation ('largely rebuilt' 0.03, 'enjoyed a busy season' 0.15); 'rarely remembered' / 'often overlooked' only 0.09-0.12. Near misses keep 'but largely' and 'recently enjoyed' in non-reputation uses.
